examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Standardize a normal variable with Z=(X−μ)/σ, using standard deviation rather than variance. Symmetry makes mean, median and mode coincide. Tail probabilities require a table, supplied CDF values or an exact symmetry argument. Linear transformations preserve normality. Sums of independent normals have added means and variances. Normal tails extend indefinitely, so finite standard-deviation intervals never contain all probability.

**Key relationship:** Z=(X−μ)/σ; Z~N(0,1)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Read μ and σ² carefully.
2. Standardize event endpoints.
3. Use symmetry and supplied CDF values with correct tails.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify μ and σ² by comparing both the prefactor and exponent with the standard normal density. Standardize using Z=(X−μ)/σ. Symmetry gives equal tail probabilities around μ. Scaling by a negative value reverses inequality direction when transforming a probability, even though the resulting distribution is still normal.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
X is normal with mean 10 and variance 9. What is P(X≤10)?

**Answer: 0.5.** A normal density is symmetric about its mean and has no atom at the mean. Therefore half the total area lies to its left: P(X≤10)=1/2. The variance 9 means standard deviation 3, but standardization at the mean is zero regardless.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Variance is σ², while the denominator in Z uses σ. Poisson and binomial variables are discrete and are not exactly normal merely because a normal approximation is available.

In N(μ,σ²), the second parameter is variance; take its square root when standardizing.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

X has normal mean 10, variance 4. z-score at 14?

- **A.** 4
- **B.** 7
- **C.** 1
- **D.** 2

**Answer: D.** σ=2, so z=(14−10)/2=2.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

A nondegenerate normal law has:

- **A.** Symmetry about its mean
- **B.** Mean equal to median
- **C.** All mass within one standard deviation
- **D.** Zero probability at each finite point

**Answer: A, B, D.** A/B follow from symmetry; D holds for continuous distributions. Tails refute C.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Independent normals have variances 9 and 16. Standard deviation of their sum?



**Answer: 5.** Independent variances add to 25; take the square root to obtain 5.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q14 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/normal-distribution?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Normal distribution. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Compare f(x)=1/(3√(2π))·exp(−x²/18) with the normal density 1/(σ√(2π))·exp(−(x−μ)²/(2σ²)).
2. Here μ=0 and σ=3, since 2σ²=18. The density is continuous over the full real line.
3. X is a **normal variable, B**, not the discrete Poisson or a constant-density uniform variable.
